problem: Earlier VLN pre-training either drops action prediction entirely (VLN-BERT and AirBERT only do instruction–trajectory compatibility or matching) or predicts a single-step action from the current panorama alone (PREVALENT). None of them use the trajectory history, and none explicitly model the temporal order of instructions or observations.
motivation: VLN is a POMDP, so decisions depend on past observations. It is also spatio-temporal and sensitive to the order of the trajectory, so representations should encode history and temporal order, not just global visual–text matching. The authors argue that the pre-training objectives should be VLN-specific and aligned with the final goal of next-action prediction.
key_idea: Pre-train an LXMERT-style VLN transformer on instruction–trajectory pairs with history- and order-aware proxy tasks: Trajectory Order Modeling, Group Order Modeling, and Action Prediction with History. These are added to MLM and Trajectory-Instruction Matching, and the model is then fine-tuned as a RecBERT-style recurrent agent.
insight:
Table 5 (val-unseen) shows the pieces are complementary.
- MLM alone lifts R2R SR from 54.19 to 60.75.
- Each VLN-specific task adds on top of MLM. APH helps most: R2R SR/SPL 62.01/56.13 and REVERIE SPL 23.76, versus MLM-only 60.75/54.81 and 21.83.
- APH beats history-free AP on every metric: R2R 62.01/56.13 vs 61.27/55.68, NDH GP 3.88 vs 3.83. APH also converges faster in pre-training action accuracy (figure).
- All five tasks together give the best result: R2R 63.86/57.07, REVERIE RGSPL 15.31, NDH GP 4.37.
- Adding the processed BnB image-caption sequences mainly helps object-centric REVERIE (SPL 25.10→26.11, RGSPL 15.31→15.73), while R2R and NDH stay about flat. The authors attribute this to BnB captions describing rooms and objects.
method: Architecture: LXMERT-like two-stream transformer. It has a 9-layer language encoder (WordPiece tokens + position embeddings), a 1-layer vision encoder and a 3-layer cross-modal encoder with bidirectional cross-attention (layer counts follow PREVALENT). Each image is a 2048-d ImageNet ResNet-152 feature concatenated with a 128-d heading/elevation encoding ([sin, cos] repeated 32×), giving 2176-d.
Trajectory visual input: for order modeling, pre-training uses the sequence of front-view images along the path rather than panoramas, because adjacent panoramas in the same room look too similar.

MLM and TIM: MLM masks 15% of instruction tokens conditioned on the trajectory. TIM is a binary instruction–trajectory match on the [CLS] token, with 50% negatives drawn from the same environment so the model must distinguish paths rather than houses.
Trajectory Order Modeling (TOM): 50% of the trajectory images are shuffled. An FC+softmax head on each cross-modal visual output classifies that image's original position (N-way).

Group Order Modeling (GOM): the trajectory is split evenly into two sub-trajectory groups G1 and G2, separated by [SEP]. A 3-way classification on [CLS] decides whether G2 comes after G1, before G1, or is a random group from another trajectory (1/3 probability each).

Action Prediction with History (APH): given the instruction, the history front-view trajectory v1..v_{t-1} and the current 36-view panorama, an FC head on [CLS] classifies which of the 36 views is the next view.

Pre-training data and fine-tuning: pre-training uses PREVALENT's augmented R2R (104K original + 6482K synthesized) plus 342K processed BnB image-sequence/caption pairs (captionless images removed, 5-7 images per path). One task is sampled per mini-batch; 4×V100, AdamW, lr 5e-5, 15 epochs. Fine-tuning uses a RecBERT-style recurrent [CLS] state, with both vision and language weights transferred.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer (9 text / 1 vision / 3 cross-modal layers) pre-trained with HOP objectives, fine-tuned as a RecBERT (VLN↻BERT)-style recurrent agent; ImageNet ResNet-152 visual features (frozen feature extractor)
setting.training_data: Pre-training: PREVALENT augmented R2R (104K original + 6482K speaker-synthesized samples) and, for HOP(2), 342K processed BnB (Airbnb) image-sequence/caption pairs. Fine-tuning: each downstream task's training set; R2R additionally uses PREVALENT augmented data.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, ResNet-152 features + orientation) with candidate navigable views; pre-training uses front-view image trajectories
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select among navigable candidates)
setting.privileged: none (standard REVERIE setting with benchmark-provided object bounding boxes for grounding)

numbers_note:
Tables look complete. The paper also reports HOP (0), the same architecture without pre-training, as a baseline; it is omitted above (e.g., R2R test-unseen SR 55 / SPL 50).

The ablation Table 5 (val-unseen) gives more precise R2R numbers: Model 9 = HOP(1) SR 63.86 / SPL 57.07, and Model 10 = HOP(2) SR 63.52 / SPL 57.22.

There is a small inconsistency on REVERIE val-unseen HOP(1) RGS: 18.23 in Table 3 vs 18.35 in Table 5.

On NDH, GP is given under three settings; the Mixed setting is stored as 'GP'.

On RxR, SPL/nDTW/sDTW are printed as fractions and were converted to 0-100. The RxR evaluation is English-only.

The variant behind the appendix nDTW/CLS table is not specified.

The headline numbers mix variants: 59 SPL on R2R and 24.34 SPL on REVERIE come from HOP(2), while 3.31 GP on NDH comes from HOP(1).
results:
On R2R test-unseen, HOP(2) reaches SR 64 / SPL 59 (HOP(1): 64 / 58), above the strongest pre-trained baselines RecBERT (63 / 57) and AirBERT (62 / 57). Removing pre-training (HOP(0)) drops this to 55 / 50.

On REVERIE test-unseen, HOP(2) reaches SPL 24.34 and RGSPL 14.34, versus RecBERT 23.99 / 13.51 and AirBERT 23.61 / 13.28; its SR (30.17) is slightly below AirBERT's (30.28).

On NDH test-unseen (Mixed), HOP(1) reaches GP 3.31 versus ORIST's 3.15. On RxR-English val-unseen, HOP(2) reaches SR 42.3 / sDTW 0.33 versus EnvDrop+Syntax at 39.2 / 0.32.
limitations: Pre-training is computationally expensive (acknowledged by the authors).
Evaluated only on indoor, discrete nav-graph (Matterport3D) tasks; no continuous or outdoor environments and no real robot.
No masked image modeling objectives. Gains over RecBERT/AirBERT are modest (about 1-2 SPL), and pre-training uses front-view trajectories while fine-tuning uses panoramas.
